title: CCSS social security for independent workers
text: Independent workers (trabajadores independientes) with income must be affiliated with the CCSS and contribute to health and maternity (SEM) and pensions (IVM) on a declared reference income (ingreso de referencia). The state subsidizes part of the contribution; the lower the income bracket, the larger the subsidy. The CCSS has used tax information from Hacienda to compute retroactive charges for unregistered independents, which has been litigated (Abogado Tributario, 2026).
keywords: obligación de afiliarse a la CCSS como trabajador independiente, seguro de salud SEM y pensiones IVM, ingreso de referencia, cobros retroactivos
status: vigente (escala por confirmar con la CCSS)

title: CCSS social security for independent workers
text:
- Each contractor client (for example GrantFox's 7 contractors) must handle their own CCSS as independents; Fact3 can estimate the monthly contribution from declared income, but the CCSS bills it.
- **Reclassification risk:** if a "contractor" works under subordination (fixed hours, exclusivity, direction by the company), the CCSS can treat the relationship as employment and charge the company employer contributions retroactively. Flag this to company clients that rely on many full-time contractors.
- Income tax deduction: CCSS contributions paid by an independent are generally treated as a deductible expense for the ISU; confirm with the accountant.

title: Tax treatment of crypto assets in Costa Rica
text:
Dated August 23, 2023. Because the Banco Central de Costa Rica does not recognize crypto as legal tender, the DGT treats it as **virtual assets, which are intangible assets** ("activos virtuales (activos intangibles)"). It is not money and not a foreign currency for tax purposes.

The oficio is an answer to a consultation, so under art. 119 CNPT it is **informative, not binding** (see [[authority-and-sources]]).
keywords: criptomonedas no son moneda de curso legal, activo intangible, activo virtual, posición de la DGT, oficio MH-DGT-OF-0460-2023, no vinculante

sources.label: EY, DGT issues ruling on tax treatment of crypto assets (MH-DGT-OF-0460-2023)
Delfino, government presents bills to tax foreign income (Bill 25.796)

title: Tax treatment of crypto assets in Costa Rica
text:
| Situation | Tax | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gains from buying and selling crypto held as personal wealth (investor) | IRCGPC, capital gains | 15% on the gain (see [[renta-capital]]) |
| Returns from crypto investments (yield, staking-like returns) | IRCGPC, capital income | 15% |
| Crypto tied to a lucrative activity (trading business, a company's treasury used in its business) | ISU | Progressive or corporate rates (see [[renta-territoriality]]) |
| Commissions for organizing, verifying or exchanging virtual assets (exchanges, brokers, validators acting as a business) | ISU | Ordinary rates |

**Getting paid in crypto for work** is ordinary business income (ISU) valued in colones on the date received. The later sale or swap of that crypto is a second event that can produce a gain or loss, measured from the value at receipt.
keywords: impuesto sobre la renta de criptomonedas, cobrar o recibir pago en cripto USDC por trabajo es ingreso ordinario, vender cripto con ganancia como inversionista paga 15%, trading como negocio, comisiones

title: Tax treatment of crypto assets in Costa Rica
text: Services related to virtual assets, including buying and selling them, are subject to IVA, and so are the commissions on those services. The crypto itself is not a taxable "sale of goods" for the holder; the IVA lands on the service provider's fee.

title: Tax treatment of crypto assets in Costa Rica
text:
- A Costa Rica-resident provider of crypto services earns Costa Rican-source ISU income.
- A non-resident providing a crypto service to a Costa Rica resident, with direct effect in Costa Rica, triggers the impuesto sobre remesas al exterior (see [[remesas-exterior]]).
- **Open question for Fact3:** whether a gain realized on a foreign exchange by a resident investor is Costa Rican-source at all. The territorial principle suggests foreign gains are out of scope, but the DGT has not addressed it directly. Get a written legal opinion before selling crypto tax filings (already flagged in the MVP plan).

title: Tax treatment of crypto assets in Costa Rica
text: In September 2026 the government presented Bill **25.796** to tax foreign-source passive income and capital gains, plus a second bill to cut exemptions (Delfino). TRIBU-CR already has codes 119 to 124 for "rentas pasivas de fuente extranjera". Until the bill passes and its text is confirmed, treat foreign passive income and gains as untaxed under the territorial system, and keep the classification rules dated so they can switch on a given effective date.

title: Tax treatment of crypto assets in Costa Rica
section: Practical rules for the Fact3 ledger
text:
1. Value every crypto event in colones on its date: stablecoins at their USD value, then the BCCR CRC/USD rate for that day; other assets from a price feed.
2. Keep cost basis per lot so gains can be computed for the IRCGPC (15%) or the ISU.
3. Transfers between a client's own wallets and exchange accounts are not taxable events.
4. Swaps crypto to crypto are disposals (the DGT treats crypto as an asset, so a swap realizes a gain or loss).
5. Exchange and custody fees charged by a Costa Rican provider carry 13% IVA.

title: Electronic invoicing version 4.4
text:
- Factura electrónica (sale to an identified buyer)
- Tiquete electrónico (sale to a final consumer without a tax ID)
- Nota de crédito and nota de débito electrónicas (corrections)
- **Factura electrónica de compra** (the buyer issues it: purchases from simplified-regime sellers, and since 4.4 also services and intangibles bought from foreign providers without Costa Rican domicile, including the IVA)
- **Factura electrónica de exportación** (sales to foreign buyers, see [[iva-exports]])
- **Recibo electrónico de pago** (new in 4.4, see below)
- Mensaje receptor (the buyer's acceptance, partial acceptance or rejection of a received invoice)

Each document is a signed XML with a **50-digit numeric key** (clave), sent to Hacienda when issued; Hacienda answers with an acceptance or rejection message. Records are kept 5 years.

title: Electronic invoicing version 4.4
text:
1. **Payment methods:** new fields and codes to report digital payments such as SINPE Móvil and other platforms, so Hacienda can trace them.
2. **Combos and packages:** the seller must break down items bundled into a package.
3. **Discounts:** ten discount type codes (loyalty, volume, seasonal, promotional, commercial, other, and more) instead of a free-text description.
4. **Purchase invoice extended:** factura electrónica de compra now covers services and intangibles bought from foreign providers, with the import IVA included. Not for tangible goods that go through customs.
5. **Recibo electrónico de pago (REP):** for credit sales by independent professionals and small and medium businesses (not large taxpayers). It lets them pay the IVA when the customer pays rather than when invoicing (credit sales up to 90 days).

title: Legal hierarchy, binding force and where official texts live
text:
Answer tax questions by citing the highest norm that settles them, in this order:

1. **Constitución Política** and international treaties (tax treaties are few for Costa Rica).
2. **Laws (leyes)** passed by the Asamblea Legislativa. The core ones for Fact3:
   - Ley 9635, Ley de Fortalecimiento de las Finanzas Públicas (2018). Título I is the Ley del Impuesto sobre el Valor Agregado (IVA). Título II reformed the Ley del Impuesto sobre la Renta.
   - Ley 7092, Ley del Impuesto sobre la Renta (as amended by Ley 9635).
   - Ley 4755, Código de Normas y Procedimientos Tributarios (CNPT): procedure, sanctions, consultations, record keeping.
   - Ley 17, Ley Constitutiva de la CCSS, plus CCSS regulations for social security.
3. **Reglamentos (decretos ejecutivos)**: Reglamento de la Ley del IVA, Reglamento de la Ley del Impuesto sobre la Renta, and yearly decrees that update brackets (for 2026, Decreto 45333-H).
4. **Resoluciones de alcance general** from the Dirección General de Tributación (DGT), numbered MH-DGT-RES-NNNN-YYYY (older ones DGT-R-NNN-YYYY). They bind taxpayers and the administration. Examples: MH-DGT-RES-0027-2024 (e-invoicing v4.4), MH-DGT-RES-0017-2023 (export-related IVA exemptions), MH-DGT-RES-0010-2026 (TRIBU-CR deadlines).
5. **Oficios / respuestas a consultas** (MH-DGT-OF-NNNN-YYYY): DGT answers to a specific taxpayer's question.
keywords: jerarquía de normas tributarias, Constitución, leyes, reglamentos, decretos ejecutivos, resoluciones generales de la DGT, oficios, qué norma prevalece, Ley 9635, Ley 7092, Código de Normas y Procedimientos Tributarios

title: IVA on exports of services and goods
text:
Article 8 of the IVA law exempts:

- **Inciso 1:** exports of goods and the operations related to them, and services provided by taxpayers "cuando se utilicen fuera del ámbito territorial del impuesto" (used outside Costa Rica's tax territory).
- **Inciso 2:** "Las ventas de bienes o servicios para la exportación" and sales between free-zone beneficiaries.

For Fact3 this is the key rule for freelancers and companies that bill foreign clients (for example a Costa Rican developer invoicing a US company or a foundation such as SDF): if the service is **used outside Costa Rica**, it is exempt from IVA, but it is still a taxable operation for reporting.
keywords: exención del IVA en exportaciones, artículo 8 Ley 9635, servicios usados fuera de Costa Rica, cliente extranjero, no se cobra IVA al cliente del exterior

EY, DGT resolution on export-related services exempt from IVA (MH-DGT-RES-0017-2023)

title: IVA on exports of services and goods
text: The test is where the service is used or consumed, not where the provider sits or where payment comes from. A software service delivered to a foreign company for its business abroad is generally exported. A service to a foreign company that is consumed in Costa Rica (for example, work on a Costa Rican branch's local operations) may not be. Get the accountant's sign-off on edge cases and keep evidence: the contract, the client's foreign address and tax ID, and proof of foreign payment.
keywords: cuándo se considera que un servicio se usa en el exterior, pruebas y evidencia, contrato, dirección e identificación fiscal del cliente extranjero, pagos del exterior, casos dudosos

title: IVA on exports of services and goods
text:
- Exporters are IVA taxpayers by law (art. 4) and must be registered.
- Each export is documented with a **factura electrónica de exportación** (v4.4 comprobante type), not a regular invoice. See [[facturacion-electronica-v44]].
- Exports are declared in the monthly IVA return (TRIBU-CR form 150) even if no IVA is due.
- IVA paid on inputs used for exports keeps its right to credit, and if credits pile up the exporter can request a refund; taxpayers with credit-eligible operations above 75% can use the expedited refund in art. 28.

title: IVA (value added tax) basics under Ley 9635
text:
IVA applies to the sale of goods and the provision of services in Costa Rica: "Se establece un impuesto sobre el valor agregado en la venta de bienes y en la prestación de servicios". Services supplied by a provider abroad are also taxed when the recipient is an IVA taxpayer located in Costa Rica (art. 1, "cuando el destinatario sea un contribuyente del artículo 4 de esta ley y esté ubicado en el territorio de la República"). That is the reverse charge case: the Costa Rican buyer self-assesses the IVA.

In e-invoicing v4.4 the buyer documents this with a **factura electrónica de compra**, now extended to services and intangibles bought from foreign companies with no Costa Rican domicile, including the IVA (see [[facturacion-electronica-v44]]).

title: IVA (value added tax) basics under Ley 9635
text: Anyone who habitually sells goods or provides services is a taxpayer. The law adds that all **exporters** and everyone in the **régimen de tributación simplificada** are taxpayers ("son contribuyentes todos los exportadores y los que se acojan al régimen de tributación simplificada"). A freelancer who only exports services must still register for IVA, issue export invoices and file the monthly return.

text: Under v4.4, independent professionals and small and medium businesses that sell on credit can defer paying the IVA until they are paid (credit terms up to 90 days), documenting the payment with the new **recibo electrónico de pago** (Deloitte summary of MH-DGT-RES-0027-2024). Large taxpayers are excluded. Confirm the exact conditions in the resolution before building on it.

title: Simplified tax regime (régimen de tributación simplificada)
text:
- **Art. 35:** the tax administration "podrá establecer regímenes de tributación simplificada de acceso voluntario" for small taxpayers in specific activities. The regulation sets which activities qualify and the income and purchase limits.
- **Art. 38:** returns are filed **quarterly**, "dentro de los primeros quince días naturales siguientes al trimestre respectivo".
- **Art. 40:** in some cases these taxpayers do not have to issue invoices, but must give a receipt when the buyer asks. Buyers who need a deductible document issue a **factura electrónica de compra** (see [[facturacion-electronica-v44]]).
- **Art. 41:** simplified-regime taxpayers **cannot use IVA input credits**.
- **Art. 4:** they are IVA taxpayers.
keywords: régimen de tributación simplificada, acceso voluntario, declaración trimestral, no puede usar crédito fiscal del IVA, no emite factura en algunos casos, artículos 35 a 43

title: Simplified tax regime (régimen de tributación simplificada)
text: The regime targets small retail and similar activities listed in the regulation (recent additions included pastry making, succulent sales and costume jewelry, per El Observador). Professional services such as software development and freelancers who export services are generally **not** eligible, and exporters gain nothing from it because they lose the input credit. Default assumption for Fact3: clients are in the general regime (form 150 monthly, 101 annually) unless the accountant confirms otherwise. Pull the current list of eligible activities and limits from the regulation (pending, see PwC 2025 reform).

title: TRIBU-CR platform and declaration codes
text:
TRIBU-CR is Hacienda's integrated tax platform. It went live on **October 6, 2025**, replacing ATV, TRAVI and DeclaraWeb; returns are filed only there, through the Oficina Virtual (OVi). There is no public filing API: in the Fact3 MVP the accountant files drafts by hand.

Declarations moved from "D-xxx" codes to three-digit codes. Old D-numbers can be ambiguous (for example the old informative D-151 is now 270, while the new 151 is an agricultural IVA return), so always use the new code.
keywords: qué es TRIBU-CR, reemplazó ATV, Oficina Virtual OVi, 6 de octubre de 2025, sin API para declarar

title: Withholding on payments abroad (impuesto sobre remesas al exterior)
text: When a Costa Rican payer (company or individual with an activity) pays, credits or makes available Costa Rican-source income to a **non-resident**, the payer must withhold the impuesto sobre remesas al exterior (art. 59, Ley 7092) and pay it to Hacienda. The DGT crypto ruling also says that a non-resident providing services with a direct effect in Costa Rica to a resident triggers this tax.

title: Capital income and capital gains (IRCGPC)
text:
Since Ley 9635 (in force July 1, 2019) Costa Rica has a dual system:

- **ISU (Impuesto sobre las Utilidades):** profits from a lucrative activity, progressive rates (see [[renta-territoriality]]).
- **IRCGPC (Impuesto sobre las Rentas de Capital y las Ganancias y Pérdidas de Capital):** passive income and gains from assets **not** tied to a lucrative activity. It has three parts: rentas de capital inmobiliario (rent), rentas de capital mobiliario (interest, dividends and similar), and ganancias y pérdidas de capital (gains on sale of assets).

If the asset is tied to the taxpayer's lucrative activity, the income goes into the ISU instead, at ordinary rates.
keywords: diferencia entre rentas de capital y utilidades, impuesto sobre rentas de capital y ganancias y pérdidas de capital IRCGPC, inversiones pasivas, alquileres, intereses, dividendos

title: Capital income and capital gains (IRCGPC)
text:
- Capital income and capital gains: **15%** general rate. For capital gains it applies to the difference between the transfer value and the acquisition value (El Observador).
- **2.25% option:** for assets acquired **before July 1, 2019**, the seller may instead pay 2.25% on the total transfer value. It is optional.
- Exempt example: the sale of the taxpayer's **vivienda habitual** (habitual residence). Other exemptions and the reduced rates for specific instruments are in Ley 7092 chapter XI; add them from the primary text (pending).
keywords: tarifa de ganancias de capital 15%, opción 2,25% sobre el valor de venta para bienes adquiridos antes de julio 2019, venta de inmueble, vivienda habitual exenta

title: Income tax on profits (ISU), territoriality and 2026 brackets
text: Costa Rica taxes only **Costa Rican-source income**. Art. 1 of the income tax law (as reformed by Ley 9635): "se entenderá por rentas, ingresos, o beneficios de fuente costarricense, los generados en el territorio nacional". Income from services is sourced where the work is performed, so a resident freelancer working from Costa Rica for a foreign client has Costa Rican-source income, even if paid abroad in USD or crypto. Purely foreign passive income (dividends, interest, gains on foreign assets) has historically been outside the scope; bills to tax it are pending (see [[crypto-assets]] and [[renta-capital]]).
keywords: principio de territorialidad, renta de fuente costarricense, ingresos del exterior, trabajo hecho en Costa Rica para clientes extranjeros, rentas pasivas del extranjero

title: Income tax on profits (ISU), territoriality and 2026 brackets
section: Fiscal period, annual return and partial payments
text:
- The fiscal period is the calendar year (January 1 to December 31).
- The annual return is due by **March 15** of the following year: TRIBU-CR form **101** (individual), **102** (legal entity), 103 (public entity). These replaced the old D-101.
- **Partial payments (pagos parciales):** three advance payments during the year, the last one due December 31 (El Observador). The usual schedule is the last business days of June, September and December, each a share of the prior year's tax. Confirm the exact computation with the accountant before automating reminders.
